newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-DI STEFANO CRITICISES NEW CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DI STEFANO CRITICISES NEW CHAMPIONS' LEAGUE.

text.p: Former Real Madrid great Alfredo Di Stefano has criticised the new-look European Cup "Champions' League" as a competition dominated by interests off the field.

"This Cup, now open to all including those who are not national champions, has little to do with sport and too much to do with interests," Di Stefano, 70, told Italy's La Gazzetta dello Sport daily newspaper in an interview.
"One can lose twice to the same opponent, at home and away, and still win the trophy.
"The thrill of the Cup was the matches with immediate elimination, with one's chest bared. He who is hit dies," the former Argentine and Spanish international said.
With Di Stefano up front, Real won the European Cup five times in a row from 1955-56 to 1959-60, an unrivalled achievement, and the Spanish league title eight times.

From next season, the European Cup has been opened to the top two clubs from the continent's main soccer powers. Newcastle United, for example, will represent England alongside champions Manchester United despite having not not won the domestic league title since 1927.
